sections.overview: The Tasmanian devil is the largest living carnivorous marsupial and is now native only to Tasmania.
sections.identification: Its toothy gape and loud screeches make it distinctive.
sections.habitat: It uses coastal heath, open dry forests and mixed forest-rainforest habitats.
sections.diet: It eats a wide range of animal prey and is also a major scavenger, consuming carcasses communally.
sections.behavior: It is mainly nocturnal, sheltering by day and searching for food at night.
sections.reproduction: The sources used for this brief profile do not give a concise reproductive summary.
sections.ecology: Devil facial tumour disease is a transmissible cancer spread through biting and has caused severe declines in affected populations.
sections.conservation: Tasmania lists the species as Endangered and coordinates a dedicated recovery program.
